listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, October 17, 2026. The lead story is about Russia sanctions. The U.S. president has temporarily ended many restrictions on Moscow that Congress recently passed, citing national security concerns. The move comes as a dispute between Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy intensifies. Trump has said the Ukrainian leader is more difficult to deal with than Putin. Zelenskyy has been rallying support in the European Union. Now the front page. Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday. Several people were hurt, including a Washington Post photojournalist. Hot winds are fueling a fast-moving fire in Southern California. It has burned coastal homes, and thousands have been told to evacuate. Ukraine has resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries after a brief truce that Zelenskyy said Moscow had spurned. The FBI and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating suspicious mailings sent to election officials and congressional offices. Now the sections. In Tech and AI, Anthropic's Compliance API now returns saved Claude instructions for Enterprise organizations, in beta. In Politics, White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is transitioning out, less than a week after she started. In World, protests in New Delhi have intensified over a review of voter lists. In Sports, Alexander Volkanovski has called for a superfight against Justin Gaethje. In Atlanta, Donald Trump rallied Republicans in Dalton on Friday. In Architecture, Autodesk is pushing a connected AI assistant. In Science and Nature, Brazil's Amazon deforestation fell 42 percent to a record low. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
lead.note: The US president has temporarily ended many restrictions on Moscow that Congress recently passed, citing national security concerns. The move comes as a dispute between Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy intensifies. The waiver covers many restrictions, though the summary does not list which ones are affected or for how long beyond the word temporarily. Reporting this week has also described Zelenskyy's growing rift with the United States, Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian refineries, and Russian strikes that left hundreds of thousands without power in Ukraine. Congress passed the restrictions recently, so the waiver sets the executive branch's position against that legislation. For a reader following world affairs, this is the main development to watch, since it shapes the pressure on Moscow and the relationship between Washington and Kyiv at the same time.
lead.headline: Trump Waives Several Russia Sanctions Amid Zelensky Row
decks: Temporary waiver covers many restrictions Congress recently passed on Moscow
